The *Gūthakhādakapetivatthu* ("The Excrement Eating Female Ghost") is a short narrative verse text included in the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali canon. In this discourse, a female ghost (*petī*) explains the karmic retribution that led to her wretched condition, revealing that her torment and foul sustenance arose from associating with an evil monk.

 Automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus demonstrates substantial textual overlap within the Pali tradition, particularly with its commentary, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, which shares extensive passages with the text [DharmaNexus]. In addition, the text shares nearly its entire verse sequence (§0.1–9.1) with the preceding narrative, the *Gūthakhādakapetavatthu* (Pv 43), displaying a 0.98 similarity match [DharmaNexus]. Further formulaic verses are shared with other stories in the collection, including the *Seriṇīpetivatthu* (Pv 31, §2.1–3.3) and the *Sāṇavāsītherapetavatthu* (Pv 27, §2.1–2.4) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also reports low-scoring cross-language alignments with a Tibetan Buddhist canonical text, although this is an uncurated machine result rather than an established parallel [DharmaNexus].
